## OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-05: fix the gate, REPORT what it newly flags, do not triage

Scope for whoever implements this: fix the name-resolution defect so a read is resolved to its
OWNING dataclass rather than matched as a bare attribute name anywhere under src/rebar. Then
run the fixed gate across the whole schema and REPORT the newly-flagged fields.

Do NOT triage them. Each newly-flagged field is a wire-it-or-delete-it product judgment — the
same call the operator made individually for dce2 (delete) and a573 (delete). An agent must
not make those unsupervised inside a gate fix.

Practical consequence to plan for: the fixed gate will likely fail CI on the fields it newly
flags, so landing the fix and resolving those fields may need sequencing. Options are to land
the fix with accurate `# read-via:` markers naming a tracking ticket for each newly-flagged
field (the mechanism the codebase already uses), or to land it behind the field resolutions.
Choose one and say which; do not silently exempt a field to make CI green.

Known instance already ruled on: `CodeHealthConfig.enabled` is being REMOVED under bug
a573-00ea-2bf6-4eb1, so it should not appear in the residual list once that lands.

comments.body:
## RCA + fix report (rebar-debug, 2026-08-05)

### Proven root cause

`scripts/check_config_reads.py::_collect_reads` returned a GLOBAL `set[str]` of terminal
attribute names read anywhere under `src/rebar`, and `check()` tested `field_name in reads`.
A field was therefore satisfied by any same-named attribute on any unrelated object.

### Discriminating proof (RED-first, synthetic)

Two dataclasses declaring the same bare field name, only one of them read:

```
CodeHealthConfig.enabled   <- zero reads anywhere
UiConfig.enabled           <- read once, via `cfg.ui.enabled`
```

Run against the PRE-FIX gate, the output was a single error naming `Config.code_health`
(the unread section-wiring field) — `CodeHealthConfig.enabled` was NOT reported. The live
`ui.enabled` read had put the bare name `enabled` into the one global set, silently
satisfying the inert field. That is the exact mechanism that let the real
`CodeHealthConfig.enabled` survive until a573-00ea-2bf6-4eb1 removed it, while its
uniquely-named sibling `analyzers` did trip the gate. The asymmetry is luck, not a check.

Three tests were confirmed RED for that reason against the unfixed gate (the two
owner-resolution cases returned `[]` — silently clean), and GREEN afterwards against an
oracle the implementing subagent never saw. A defect-seeded mutation (restoring bare-name
membership) returned them to RED, so the tests have teeth.

### The fix

`_collect_reads` now returns `set[tuple[class_name, attr_name]]` and the check is
`(cls_name, field_name) in reads`. A read counts only when its RECEIVER resolves to the
dataclass that DECLARES the field. Receiver resolution binds an expression to candidate
schema classes through six routes, each a live pattern in `src/rebar`: the section-attribute
name derived from the root `Config` (`Config.mcp: McpConfig`); parameter / `AnnAssign`
annotations; local alias assignment propagated to a fixed point (`m = cfg.mcp`); function
return annotations (`load_config() -> Config`); `IfExp` / `BoolOp` branch unions; and a
cross-module fixed point that binds an UNANNOTATED parameter from its call sites (the
`mcp_server` -> `_mcp_auth.build_composite_verifier(mcp_cfg)` pattern). An expression that
resolves to nothing contributes to no field.

### Newly-flagged fields — REPORTED, NOT TRIAGED (operator ruling)

The fixed gate was run across the whole schema at the current `origin/main`. It newly flags
exactly FOUR fields. Every one was traced by hand to a real consumer, so NO wire-it-or-delete-it
product judgement arises and nothing needs operator triage:

1. `McpConfig.readonly` — live. Read at `config.py` `mcp_readonly()` (`load_config().mcp.readonly`),
   which sits inside the `config.py` plumbing file the gate deliberately excludes from the read
   scan. The old gate passed it off the unrelated `ctx.readonly()` calls in `_mcp_reads.py` /
   `_mcp_writes.py`.
2. `McpConfig.allow_llm` — live. Read via the STRING key `_mcp_gate("allow_llm", fail=False)` in
   `mcp_server.py`; no attribute read exists for any resolver to find. Old gate passed it off
   `ctx.allow_llm`.
3. `McpConfig.allow_jira_sync` — live. Same string-key shape, `_mcp_gate("allow_jira_sync", ...)`.
   Old gate passed it off `ctx.allow_jira_sync`.
4. `JiraConfig.allow_insecure` — live and load-bearing: `JiraConfig.__post_init__` passes
   `self.allow_insecure` to `_validate_https_url(...)`, which is the cleartext-URL rejection added
   by bug bdb8. That read is inside `_config_schema.py`, also excluded as plumbing. The old gate
   passed it off `ReconcilerConfig.allow_insecure`, a genuinely DIFFERENT field read at
   `adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py` (the resolver now correctly credits that read to
   `ReconcilerConfig`).

Each received a FACTUAL `# read-via:` marker naming its actual reader — the same shape as the
existing `TrackerConfig.branch` marker. No field was silently exempted; if a future run flags a
field with no traceable reader, it is reported and left for the operator.

`CodeHealthConfig.enabled` does NOT appear in this list: a573-00ea-2bf6-4eb1 landed its removal
before this sweep ran, so the field no longer exists. It is recorded in the description as history
and is not an edit target here.

Marker audit: no `# read-via:` marker in the schema currently names a rebar ticket id, so there is
no marker parked against a closed ticket. (The one that did — dce2's, on `CodeHealthConfig.analyzers`
— left with that field.)

### Sequencing

Approach (a) from the operator ruling: the fix lands together with accurate markers for the four
fields, which is the mechanism the codebase already uses. Approach (b) was rejected because it
would block a correct checker behind product decisions this ticket has no standing to make, and
would leave the false-negative class live meanwhile.

### Negative fixtures

The two string-read cases named as required negative fixtures — `ReconcilerConfig.lock_lease_secs`
(getattr) and `VerifyConfig.require_plan_review_for_close` (plus its `require_plan_review_for_claim`
/ `require_completion_verification_for_close` siblings, all via `gate_enabled` string keys) — do
NOT false-fire: they are protected by their pre-existing `# read-via:` markers. A parametrized test
now pins each one's marker and the real tree's cleanliness, so a future edit that strips a marker
fails loudly instead of silently.

### Siblings

Construct sweep: the sibling gate scripts were checked for the same "bare terminal-name membership"
construct. `check_raw_git_writes.py` matches call names against an allowlist but already constrains
the receiver, and its over-match direction is fail-LOUD (more findings, never fewer), so it is not
an instance. `check_verify_gate_parity.py`, `check_server_manifest.py`, and `check_docs_index.py`
do no attribute-name matching. No siblings found.

Parity sweep: the gate has exactly one surface — the `Config-read gate` CI step. No CLI, MCP,
library, or automated-caller variant exists, so there is no channel that could have missed the rule.

## Landed + replicated

Gerrit change 1429 merged to main (rebased on submit). Both gates were green before Submit:
LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1, with zero unresolved comments.

Replication on merged main: the original report no longer reproduces. Re-running the
synthetic reproduction of the false-negative -- an inert `CodeHealthConfig.enabled` beside a
live `UiConfig.enabled` -- now yields exactly one error naming `CodeHealthConfig.enabled`,
where the pre-fix gate reported only the unrelated section-wiring field and let the inert one
through. The real tree passes the gate (`Config-read gate: OK`) and both gate test files pass
(27/27).

Residual risk and prevention:
- The resolver keys function names bare (module-agnostic), so a same-named function in another
  module can only WIDEN a binding. That direction is fail-quiet -- it can suppress a firing but
  never invent one -- so it cannot break CI on a live field. Accepted, and documented in the
  script's module docstring.
- An unresolvable receiver credits no field, which is fail-LOUD. That risk was retired
  empirically rather than by assertion: the whole tree was swept and all four newly-flagged
  fields were traced by hand to real consumers. Accepted.
- No marker in the schema currently names a ticket id, so there is no marker parked against a
  closed ticket. Reported, nothing to file.
- No sibling instances of the construct were found in the other gate scripts, and the gate has
  a single surface (the Config-read CI step), so the parity census has no MISSING slot.

compiled_state.description:
## The defect

`scripts/check_config_reads.py` (the 6754 gate, wired as the "Config-read gate" step at
`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:506-509`) is meant to fail CI when a `_config_schema.py`
dataclass field has no read site unless it carries a `# read-via:` marker. It does not do that.

`_collect_reads` (script lines ~84-101) builds a GLOBAL SET of attribute NAMES read anywhere under
`src/rebar`, then the check is effectively `field_name in reads` -- NOT `Class.field`.

So any field whose bare name is read on ANY other object anywhere in the tree passes the gate,
regardless of whether that field itself is ever read.

## Confirmed instance (historical -- the field has since been removed)

`CodeHealthConfig.enabled` had ZERO read sites, yet passed the gate and carried no `# read-via:`
marker, because `.enabled` is read on unrelated configs (`UiConfig.enabled` at
`_config_schema.py:416`, `McpConfig.auth_enabled`, `EnsureConfig.hint_enabled`, and several under
`llm/`). Contrast the also-removed `CodeHealthConfig.analyzers`, whose bare name was read NOWHERE in
the tree, so it DID trip the gate and needed an explicit `# read-via: inert pending bug
dce2-b93d-4112-451c` marker to keep CI green.

That asymmetry is the tell: the gate catches an inert field only when its name happens to be
globally unique. That is luck, not a check.

**Re-baselined 2026-08-05.** `CodeHealthConfig.enabled` was REMOVED under `a573-00ea-2bf6-4eb1`
(Gerrit change 1422), which merged into `origin/main` at `859b6797d9`; `CodeHealthConfig` now
declares only `scan_roots` / `size_cap` / `size_near_fraction` (`_config_schema.py:534-539`). So the
flagship instance is no longer reproducible on the live tree and is recorded here as history. It is
NOT an edit target for this ticket, and no marker is placed on it. The defect itself is unchanged
and is reproduced instead by a synthetic fixture (see the RED-first AC below), which is the more
durable proof anyway because it does not depend on any particular field surviving in the schema.

## Why this matters beyond one field

This is a FALSE-NEGATIVE class, not a single miss. Common field names -- `enabled`, `path`,
`timeout`, `remote`, `branch`, `mode` -- are exactly the ones most likely to be reused across
configs and therefore exactly the ones this gate cannot police. The inert-config family it exists
to prevent (281f, 9d7a, dce2, a573) is precisely the family it will keep missing.

## SCOPE (operator ruling, 2026-08-05) -- fix the gate, REPORT what it flags, do NOT triage

The operator has ruled on scope. It is recorded here in the DESCRIPTION (not only in a comment)
because the plan reviewer reads the description:

**In scope.** Fix the name-resolution defect so a read is resolved to its OWNING dataclass rather
than matched as a bare attribute name anywhere under `src/rebar`. Then run the fixed gate across
the whole schema and REPORT the newly-flagged fields.

**Explicitly OUT of scope: triaging the newly-flagged fields.** Each newly-flagged field is a
wire-it-or-delete-it PRODUCT judgement -- the same call the operator made individually for
`dce2-b93d-4112-451c` (delete) and `a573-00ea-2bf6-4eb1` (delete). Rationale: an agent must not make
those calls unsupervised inside a gate fix. Deleting or wiring a config field changes user-visible
behaviour, and that decision belongs to the operator, not to a side effect of a checker correction.
This ticket reports the list and stops.

**Sequencing (the practical consequence).** A stricter gate can fail CI on the fields it newly
flags, so the fix cannot land bare. The operator sanctioned two mechanisms: (a) land the fix with
accurate `# read-via:` markers -- factual pointers for fields that ARE read through indirection, and
a tracking-ticket pointer for any field that is genuinely inert -- which is the mechanism the
codebase already uses (`TrackerConfig.branch:529`, `ReconcilerConfig.lock_lease_secs:431`, the
`VerifyConfig` gate-key trio); or (b) land the fix behind resolution of those fields.

**THIS TICKET CHOOSES (a).** Reason: (b) blocks a correct checker behind product decisions that are
not this ticket's to make, and leaves the false-negative class live meanwhile. Under (a) every
marker must be ACCURATE: it cites the real reader, or names a real open tracking ticket. Silently
exempting a field to make CI green is forbidden.

**Measured result of the sweep (prototype run on `859b6797d9`).** All four newly-flagged fields turn
out to be LIVE and read through documented indirection, so NO wire-it-or-delete-it judgement arises
and nothing needs operator triage:

Each row below has TWO distinct citations, and they must not be conflated. The
"decoy" is the OTHER object whose same-named attribute made the OLD global-name gate pass the field
-- it is NOT a read of this field and is listed only to show the false-negative mechanism. The
"actual reader" is where THIS field is genuinely consumed.

1. **`McpConfig.readonly:350`**
   - decoy (not a read of this field): `ctx.readonly()` at `_mcp_reads.py:39`, `_mcp_writes.py:39`.
   - actual reader: `config.py:423`, `mcp_readonly()` -> `load_config().mcp.readonly`. Real, but it
     lives inside the `config.py` plumbing file the gate deliberately excludes from the read scan.
   - marker to add: `# read-via: config.py mcp_readonly()`.
2. **`McpConfig.allow_llm:351`**
   - decoy: `ctx.allow_llm` at `_mcp_writes.py:42`, `_mcp_llm.py:40`.
   - actual reader: `mcp_server.py:431`, `_mcp_gate("allow_llm", fail=False)` -- a STRING key, so no
     attribute read exists for any resolver to find.
   - marker to add: `# read-via: mcp_server.py _mcp_gate string key`.
3. **`McpConfig.allow_jira_sync:352`**
   - decoy: `ctx.allow_jira_sync` at `_mcp_reads.py:39`.
   - actual reader: `mcp_server.py:435`, `_mcp_gate("allow_jira_sync", fail=False)` -- STRING key.
   - marker to add: `# read-via: mcp_server.py _mcp_gate string key`.
4. **`JiraConfig.allow_insecure:492`**
   - decoy: `adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py:121` reads `reconciler.allow_insecure`. That is a
     read of **`ReconcilerConfig.allow_insecure`**, NOT of `JiraConfig.allow_insecure` -- the alias
     `reconciler = config.reconciler` at `settings.py:101` binds it to `ReconcilerConfig`, and the
     fixed resolver correctly credits it there. It is listed here ONLY because the bare name
     collision is what let the old gate pass the Jira field.
   - actual reader: `_config_schema.py` `JiraConfig.__post_init__`, which passes
     `self.allow_insecure` to `_validate_https_url(...)`. That is a genuine, load-bearing read (it
     gates the cleartext-URL rejection added by bug bdb8) -- it simply sits inside the
     `_config_schema.py` plumbing file the gate excludes. The field is NOT inert: deleting it would
     change validation behaviour.
   - marker to add: `# read-via: _config_schema.py JiraConfig.__post_init__ url-scheme validation`.

Each therefore receives a FACTUAL `# read-via:` marker naming its ACTUAL reader (never the decoy) --
the same shape as the existing `TrackerConfig.branch:529` marker. This is documentation of a
verified read site, not a product judgement, so it stays inside the operator's ruling: no
wire-it-or-delete-it call arises for any of the four, because each was traced to a live consumer. If
a future run flags a field with no such reader, it is REPORTED and left for the operator, never
silently marked.

## Required negative fixtures (the gate must NOT false-fire on these)

A correct owning-dataclass resolver still has to tolerate legitimate STRING-keyed reads. A prior
manual sweep of all config dataclass fields (under a573) surfaced these live-but-string-read cases;
they are required negative fixtures:

- `ReconcilerConfig.lock_lease_secs:431` -- read via `getattr` in
  `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_advisory_lock.py`; already carries a `# read-via:` marker.
- `VerifyConfig.require_plan_review_for_close:163` (and its `require_plan_review_for_claim:172` /
  `require_completion_verification_for_close:159` siblings) -- read via
  `gate_enabled(root, "<key>", ...)` string keys in `_commands/gates.py`; already carry markers.

The fixed gate must leave these passing.

## Design of the fix

Replace the global name set with a per-read owner resolution in `scripts/check_config_reads.py`:

1. Parse `_config_schema.py` into `class -> {field -> annotation}` and derive the SECTION map from
   the root `Config` dataclass (`code_health -> CodeHealthConfig`, etc.).
2. For every `*.py` under `src/rebar` (keeping the existing `_config_schema.py` / `config.py`
   plumbing exclusion), resolve the RECEIVER expression of each `ast.Attribute` read to a set of
   candidate owning schema classes, using: the section-attribute name (`x.code_health` ->
   `CodeHealthConfig`), parameter/variable annotations naming a schema class, local assignment
   propagation (`m = cfg.mcp; m.readonly`), function RETURN annotations (`load_config() -> Config`),
   `IfExp` / `BoolOp` branches, and a cross-module fixed point that binds unannotated PARAMETERS
   from their call sites (`build_composite_verifier(mcp_cfg)` called with `cfg.mcp`).
3. A field is satisfied only by a read whose resolved owner set contains its declaring class.
4. After the sweep, also report any existing `# read-via:` marker whose pointer names a rebar ticket
   id, so a marker parked against a since-CLOSED ticket surfaces instead of silently persisting.
   (Verified on `859b6797d9`: zero markers currently name a ticket id -- the dce2 one left with
   `analyzers` -- so this step reports an empty list today and exists to catch the next one.)

**Failure direction, stated honestly.** An unresolvable receiver contributes to NO field, so a live
field read only through a receiver the resolver cannot bind is newly FLAGGED -- this errs FAIL-LOUD,
not fail-quiet, and a false positive here would break CI. That risk is retired empirically rather
than by assertion: the prototype was run over the whole tree at `859b6797d9` and every one of the
four newly-flagged fields was traced by hand to a real reader (table above), with no live field left
mis-flagged. The residual permissiveness is elsewhere and is fail-quiet: function names are keyed
bare (module-agnostic), so a same-named function in another module can only WIDEN a binding.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The gate resolves a read to the OWNING dataclass, not a bare attribute name -- a field is
      satisfied only by a read of that class's instance, so a same-named attribute on an unrelated
      config no longer satisfies it.
- [x] A RED-first test proves the OLD gate passes a synthetic inert field whose name is reused on an
      unrelated config, and that the fixed gate fails it. Run both versions in-process from a
      snapshot COPY of the pre-fix script -- never `git stash`, which is global across all worktrees
      sharing this host's git common dir.
- [x] BOTH existing gate test files are MIGRATED to the owner-resolution contract rather than
      worked around. They are separate files and both are explicit edit targets:
      - `tests/scripts/test_check_config_reads.py` (happy-path suite) -- its module docstring
        (lines 5-7) still declares the now-obsolete "Detection is receiver-agnostic ... terminal
        name" contract and is rewritten; its `_SCHEMA_ONE_FIELD` fixture gains a root `Config`
        dataclass + `mcp: McpConfig` section field so `cfg.mcp.ghost_knob` resolves to its owner.
      - `tests/scripts/test_check_config_reads_heldout.py` (held-out edge suite) -- its
        `test_unrelated_same_named_attribute_keeps_the_gate_quiet` currently PINS the defect as an
        "accepted trade-off" and is INVERTED to expect a firing (docstring rewritten to say why);
        its `_SCHEMA` fixture gains the same root `Config` + section field; and each receiver shape
        in `test_every_real_receiver_shape_counts_as_a_read` is kept passing by making its receiver
        resolvable (annotation, section name, alias assignment, or a call site) rather than by
        loosening the resolver. The module docstring's "receiver-agnostic detection shape" and
        "accepted fail-quiet collision trade-off" claims are rewritten too.
      Weakening the resolver to keep the old pins green is explicitly forbidden.
- [x] The two required negative fixtures above are pinned as tests over the REAL schema and still
      pass.
- [x] The gate is re-run across the whole existing `_config_schema.py` and every newly-flagged field
      is REPORTED (in a ticket comment and in the Gerrit change description). Per the operator
      ruling they are NOT triaged here.
- [x] Each newly-flagged field gets an ACCURATE `# read-via:` marker citing its real reader (the
      four in the table above), so the fix lands CI-green without a silent exemption. A field with
      no reader would instead be reported and left for the operator.
- [x] Any `# read-via:` marker whose pointer names a rebar ticket id is reported (design step 4);
      today that list is empty.
- [x] The real tree passes the fixed gate (`python scripts/check_config_reads.py` exits 0), and
      `make lint` / `make typecheck` / the `tests/scripts` suite pass.

## Provenance

Found by a code-trace archaeology pass over the metrics/code-health system while scoping
dce2-b93d-4112-451c. The gate's own escape hatch for `analyzers` was self-referential -- the bug id
in the marker is what kept CI green -- which is legitimate, but it masked that the gate could not
have caught the neighbouring field at all.

file_impact.reason: replace the global attribute-name set with an owning-dataclass resolver
accurate # read-via: markers for the fields the fixed gate newly flags
RED-first proof that a same-named attribute on an unrelated config no longer satisfies a field
invert the pinned permissive trade-off; pin the string-read negative fixtures

compiled_state.title: The 6754 inert-config gate matches field names GLOBALLY, so a name reused by any other config hides an inert field
